problems.title: False chiral leading asymptotic
problems.locator: Theorem 1.4 equation (8) p5; chiral definition pp5,21; proof p21; domination hypotheses pp13-14
hypotheses: N positive integer tends to infinity
All partitions with length <=N, without a fixed-degree or half-height restriction
problems.core_dependency: Chiral Theorem 1.4 and its use in Corollary 6.2
problems.boundary: liminf >= phi(q)^-1+q disproves chiral theorem. Full unrestricted Theorems 1.1-1.3 not disproved. Half-height or fixed-degree repair changes the observable.

problems.title: Divergent infinite genus series and printed covering integral
problems.locator: Definition 6.1 and Corollary 6.2 equation (43) p22; proof p23; H1 formula (35) p19; attribution to Novak p21; Remark 4.6 p17
hypotheses: Nonnegative even-content coefficients over all partitions
Compact torus, compact not necessarily connected covers, simple ramifications; empty branch set allowed
Printed mass n!/|Aut(Y)| and Poisson branch distribution conditioned on even count
problems.core_dependency: Exact covering integral and claimed infinite convergence; distinct from finite-order asymptotic theorem
problems.boundary: Single rows show genus series divergent; cyclic unbranched covers show printed integral infinite. Correcting factorial and cosh normalizations does not fix genus-series divergence. Novak only proves fixed-degree convergence.

problems.title: Frobenius probability family not normalizable for g>=2
hypotheses: Unrestricted partitions with printed nonnegative weights
Single-row partition has symmetric-group dimension one
problems.core_dependency: Existence of the asserted generalized probability family
problems.boundary: Rows give factorially growing weights; the probability does not exist in this range. Conditional propositions have no instance there. Torus g=1 application and normalizable g=0 family are not invalidated.

problems.title: Lemma 4.4 exponential tail rate too strong
hypotheses: A_N=m-1, so retained event lies outside Lambda_N
problems.boundary: Ratio to q^(N/2) grows at least a positive constant times m^2(m-1)^2/4. Correct Cauchy-Schwarz rate q^(N/4) still suffices for every polynomial decay and Theorem 4.5.

problems.title: Tightness proof confuses tail union with intersection
problems.locator: Proof of Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 pp14-15; Appendix Lemma A.5 p24
hypotheses: X_M is the finite cube in partition sizes and integer magnitude
All triples in Lambda_N; bounded test f, including f=1
N=1 or empty partitions with n=M+1 supplies a concrete positive missing tail
problems.core_dependency: The sole displayed uniform-tail verification for the limiting partition function and asymptotic decoupling in Theorems 1.1 and 1.3, via Appendix Lemma A.5.
problems.boundary: Printed equality and tail verification are invalid; the explicit uniform union-bound repair is valid. This is a Major proof gap, not a counterexample to the final limiting theorems.
problems.severity_rationale: The actual core limiting derivation omits entire tails. A valid replacement proves the surviving statements, but ease of repair and survival of those statements do not lower the severity of the demonstrated core proof gap.

problems.title: Wrong sign in equation (40)
problems.boundary: D log phi<0 whereas mean size positive. Insert minus sign; preceding formula with F_1,1=phi^-1 and later moment formulas support local correction.

problems.title: Incorrect beta coordinate indices in bijection proof
problems.locator: Proposition 3.3 proof and equation (22) p12; Figure 1 p2
problems.core_dependency: Coordinate description of intended median bijection
problems.boundary: Printed beta=(3,1,0,-1,-1) is not a partition. Use number of entries below n and beta_j=n-lambda_(N+1-j); figure and (22) already support correct map. Bijection existence and Casimir identity not disproved.

overall_assessment: Chiral theorem and exact covering integral false as printed; generalized family nonexistent for g>=2; core tightness derivation has a repaired Major proof gap. Unrestricted limiting statements and finite-order expansion are not refuted. Three remaining local findings are Minor.

independent_acceptance_checks.kind: Fresh focused source/assumption/counterevidence/severity analysis; prior finite program outputs reused with initial attribution, not re-executed

checks.independent_reasoning: The source explicitly sums length<=N on pp5 and21. For column (1^N), K=-N(N-1)/2 and Casimir=1; fixing M and taking N>M prevents overlap with size<=M partitions. The ordered limits give liminf>=phi(q)^(-1)+q. A half-height or fixed-degree restriction would alter the actual theorem.
checks.scope: False chiral leading theorem; no refutation of unrestricted model.

checks.independent_reasoning: Source pp19,22,23 supplies nonnegative even content moments and the n!/Aut weight. Single rows yield exp(-tm/2+tm(m-1)/(2N))/2, whose terms do not tend to zero. Connected cyclic unbranched torus covers have degree m, Aut=m and Euler characteristic0; the empty branch event has mass1/cosh(t). Thus the printed integral dominates sum q^m(m-1)!/cosh(t). S2 is abelian, giving4 conjugacy classes of commuting pairs, each centralizer2: weighted count2 versus printed4. Novak pp17,21-23 explicitly limits absolute convergence to fixed degree and calls the summed object formal.
checks.scope: Infinite series and printed integral fail; finite-order asymptotics remain separate.

checks.independent_reasoning: A single-row partition has dimension1; for g>=2,gprime>=1 its successive weight ratio is q(m+1)^(2g-2)((m+1)/(m-1))^(2gprime-2), tending to infinity. Section5.2 asserts the general family; conditional propositions do not supply a probability when normalization diverges. g=0,1 remain normalizable.
checks.scope: Nonexistence on the stated g>=2 range, not falsity of a conditional formula for an existing law.

checks.independent_reasoning: N=2m, alpha=(1^m),beta=empty,n=0 meets the complement condition A_N=m-1. Its contribution divided by q^(N/2) grows as positive constant*m^2(m-1)^2/4. Cauchy-Schwarz instead gives q^(N/4); the polynomial conclusion actually needed by (32) is already preserved by that calculation.
checks.scope: The unnecessary stronger exponential rate fails, not the finite-order result.

checks.independent_reasoning: The pp14-15 derivation invokes Lemma A.5 and then replaces the entire complement tail by a simultaneous intersection; N=1 and empty partitions leave a positive n-tail but zero printed bound. This is the sole displayed uniform-tail verification for core Theorems1.1/1.3. The repair is verified by splitting the two partition tails (2*Cq*Zr*S_M) and the remaining n-tail, where |A-B|/N<=M/2 for N>=2 and |n+delta|>=|n|/2; N=1 has zero shift. It tends to0 uniformly.
checks.scope: Major core proof gap; repaired theorem statements survive. Repair simplicity does not determine severity.

checks.independent_reasoning: Differentiating log product_j(1-q^j) gives -sum j*q^j/(1-q^j). The source middle term in(40) has positive D log phi while the mean and Eisenstein expression are positive. The preceding F=phi^(-1) expression identifies the exact minus-sign repair.
checks.scope: Local mean identity only; no downstream damage or independent central claim is asserted.
